subcategory: structure-aware multimodal document RAG for enterprise Q&A
task: Question answering over heterogeneous enterprise documents (reports, slide decks, PDFs, HTML)
problem: Vision-centric MM-RAG (page-image embeddings such as ColPali/VisRAG) neglects explicit document structure and degrades on text-dense, table-rich report-style documents.
architecture: MM-BizRAG: document-structure-aware split routing vertical documents (reports) to layout-aware parsing (Docling) and horizontal ones (slides) to holistic page-level representations; LLM-driven artifact transformation with placeholder-based positional alignment; inference-time multimodal assembly that decouples retrieval representations from generation context; FastRAGEval single-call LLM-judge metric.
retriever: OpenAI text-embedding-3-large; cohere-embed-v4 and nomic-multimodal-embed-3b multimodal embeddings
knowledge_source: enterprise documents (PDF, DOCX, HTML, PPTX) and public benchmark documents

datasets.name: internal enterprise dataset
datasets.details: 1908 questions over 1048 documents and 20429 pages, 30 business domains

key_results: On SlideVQA, FRE-Recall gains of 3.6-6.3% over ColPali and 8.4-11.1% over VisRAG.
On FinRAGBench-V the variants exceed ColPali and VisRAG by more than 25% (up to 32% points for the best variant).
The production variant TCTE reaches recall within 1-3% points of the best configuration at roughly half the latency for vertical documents.
strengths: Shows that explicit layout parsing still matters for report-style documents where page-image retrieval degrades.
Controlled variant study isolates ingestion and embedding choices with a fixed inference stack; no fine-tuning needed.

limitations.text: Public evaluation limited to two datasets; SlideVQA slides are relatively simple compared with industry presentations.
Only 213 of the >1,100 FinRAGBench-V documents processed; multilingual capability not evaluated.
Only two open-source baselines (ColPali, VisRAG); the proprietary enterprise dataset is not released.

title: MM-BizRAG: Rethinking Multimodal Retrieval-Augmented Generation for General Purpose Enterprise Q&A
